data.summary: Since 2026-10-25, of 33 gate.passed ci events 17 have no elapsed_s and 18 no preceding gate.started (ran_by 'ddflow ci run', command 'pre-commit run ...'); 40 of 102 failed full and 166 of 363 failed selected, and 219 of 307 partial, also carry neither. So `ddflow metrics` ci n=2447 p50 8m is computed over a subset that drops most hand-recorded and ran_by outcomes, and cannot be compared across outcomes. A later `ddflow ci run` record on the same tree also doubles the outcome (fix-B31c3fd06ee: passed at 08:37 with elapsed 33.4 s, again at 08:38 with none). Expected: an outcome recorded from a finished run carries that run's elapsed_s and waited_s, and metrics reports how many outcomes it could not time.
data.title: metrics gate time for ci is biased: a pass recorded by `ddflow ci run` has no gate.started and no elapsed_s

Measured at 4fadc519c, -n 24 --durations=0, load 87: 102.5 s for this one test, 30% of the always-run list's 345 summed seconds and its wall floor (118 s). The cost is allowlist x knobs x files, so it grows faster than the code. Expected: compute dead_knobs() once in the test and hoist the alias map out of the loop. The file is in every selected ci run.

data.claim: Change size is flat, selection is flat, and active item time grew about linearly with code (small items 38-50 min to about 120 min for code x2.6). Superlinear parts: suite CPU (tests x per-test start cost, about code^1.9), fold-based commands (brief exponent about 2.4 on log size, doctor about 5), and always-run's slowest test. The largest cost today is not growth in code: 68% of claim-to-merge hours since 10-26 are parked, and main has been red in every full run since 10-28, floor 281 failures, ci pass rate 1.5%, 88% of completions forced.
data.falsifier: A fixed test sample whose CPU does not rise across commits under equal load; or a per-test duration profile of a real run showing the suite's cost concentrated in a few tests rather than a flat per-process tax.
data.mechanism: Every run_cli test starts a subprocess that imports the whole CLI; start time is linear in code (0.15 s at 33k LOC, 0.87 s at 196k) and tests are linear in code, so the product is quadratic. Workers are capped at 48 on 192 cores with one slot, so CPU converts directly to wall and queue. Fold commands rescan a log linear in time. on_merge=fast runs no tests, so repo-wide guards go red unseen.
data.probe: Scripts over .ddflow/events and .ddflow/runs; git history per day; `python -m ddflow --version` at 7 commits; 24 fixed test files at 5 commits with BLAS capped, in throwaway clones; TR.reach for every module at 6 commits; select() replay of 23 merges; always-run list with --durations=0; ddflow command timings.
data.probe_output: Tests 1,707 to 18,442; src LOC 33k to 196k. Best suite run 52 s to 1,896 s; full run about 72,000 CPU-s, n=48 on all 230 runs since 10-19. Fixed sample CPU 385, 652, 783, 850, 757 s at 76k..196k LOC (one run each, load 24 to 92). Claim-to-merge p50 45 to 255 min; files per merge p50 4 to 3. Selection 5.9-8.9% of suite files; small change replay median 4.5 files plus 22-24 always; import reach p50 12 to 2. Full fallback 18% to 25%. Always-run 118 s wall, two files 64%. brief 4.9 to 40 s, doctor 7.8 to 932 s. Full findings: session scratchpad cycle-time-findings.md. Unexplained: 72k CPU-s is above what the samples predict (28-50k); no per-test durations exist after 10-12.
data.question: How does the time to add and test one feature grow as the code grows, and which parts grow worse than linearly?
